name: What does a commercial contractor do during preconstruction?

mainEntity.name: What does a commercial contractor do during preconstruction?
mainEntity.text: What does a commercial contractor do during preconstruction?

acceptedAnswer.text: Preconstruction is the planning phase that turns a concept into a buildable project. A commercial contractor may review drawings, estimate pricing, flag constructability issues, help sequence work, identify long-lead materials, and coordinate with architects and engineers. The contractor may also help refine permit strategy, phasing, and budget assumptions before construction starts. In Los Angeles-area projects, preconstruction is especially valuable because code issues, access constraints, and permit timing can have a large effect on the schedule. For owners in Glendale, Pasadena, Burbank, and North Hollywood, this phase is where hidden risks are often identified before they become expensive field problems. Good preconstruction can reduce change orders, make bid comparisons more accurate, and improve the odds of finishing on time. It is usually the most cost-effective part of the project because it prevents expensive mistakes later.
acceptedAnswer.description: During preconstruction, a commercial contractor helps define scope, estimate costs, identify risks, review constructability, coordinate consultants, and plan the schedule. This phase often shapes permit strategy, procurement, and phasing decisions before work starts. Strong preconstruction reduces change orders and surprises during construction.
